title: PreviewArtifact
description: A reference to one durably stored generated artifact. This is the contract that lets a browser see the result of a Blender mutation without the control plane, the browser, or the job ever learning a filesystem path. NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT: there is no path, no directory, no filename, and no URL. `artifact_id` plus `project_id` is the complete address; the HTTP layer projects that into a logical URL (see services/api). A worker must not know the control plane's route shape, and the same artifact is addressed differently in different deployments (local filesystem now, object storage later), so a URL would be wrong to bake into the durable record. String identifiers must be non-blank: `minLength` alone would admit whitespace-only values, so a `\S` pattern is required alongside it.

artifact_id.description: Stable, DERIVED identity of this artifact. Derived from (project_id, job_id, artifact_type) so the same completed job always maps to the same artifact and a retry reuses it instead of accumulating duplicates. The strict pattern is also a security boundary: it is a single safe path segment by construction, so it cannot address a .blend, a journal, a recovery copy, or anything outside the artifact store.

project_id.description: Owning project. Every artifact lookup is scoped by this; artifact ids are never compared across projects.

job_id.description: The job whose verified mutation this artifact depicts. Absent for an artifact not produced by a job, such as a baseline preview taken before any change.

media_type.description: IANA media type of the stored bytes, e.g. image/png. Constrained so it can be placed in a Content-Type header without further sanitising.

width.description: Pixel width. Reported so a browser can reserve layout before the image loads.

size_bytes.description: Size of the stored bytes. Zero is invalid: an empty file is a failed render, not an artifact.

checksum.description: SHA-256 of the stored bytes, prefixed with its algorithm so a future migration is unambiguous. Used for corruption detection, test verification, and later caching/version identity. It is explicitly NOT an access credential — knowing a checksum grants nothing, and authorization is always project scope.

engine.description: Coarse, non-revealing description of what produced the artifact, e.g. BLENDER_WORKBENCH. Diagnostic only.
